algorithms.content_digest: SHA-256 over exact returned UTF-8 content after CRLF and bare CR normalization to LF. It is distinct from snapshot file-byte digests.
algorithms.authority: known canon maps to canon; known revealed maps to revealed; every other known, missing, or unknown raw status maps to preparation. accepted remains preparation.
algorithms.edge_occurrence: occurrence_order is one-based successful parse order within the source record. edge_id is 'edge_' plus lowercase SHA-256 of canonical JSON {occurrence_order,revision_id,source_record_id}. Canonical JSON uses UTF-8, sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace. Backlinks return the identical complete edge object.
algorithms.cursor: Encode {binding,digest,version} as unpadded base64url UTF-8 canonical JSON. version is 2. digest is lowercase SHA-256 over canonical JSON of binding. Every binding includes campaign_id, revision_id, tree_digest, limit, sort, direction, and a typed boundary. Generation cursors also bind revision_ordinal, sorted action and status filters, nullable record_id, and the complete descending keyset boundary. Proposal cursors bind revision_ordinal, sorted status filters, nullable record_id, and the complete descending keyset boundary. Validate encoding, closed envelope, version, digest, safe identifiers, complete binding equality, then boundary existence. The digest detects corruption and binding changes; it is not authorization.
algorithms.workflow_provenance: Generation rows must reproduce the stored source envelope digest and exact campaign or record focus binding. Proposal rows must bind one immutable proposal version to its stored generation, action, context, source digest, subject before_digest, source revision, and base revision. Missing or inconsistent stored provenance returns source_digest_conflict without content disclosure.
algorithms.workflow_summary_only: Collection items expose identifiers, exact bindings, status, ordering metadata, and retryability only. They never expose prompts, excerpts, Draft text, before or after content, table facts, audit text, provider-native events, or session identifiers.
algorithms.record_search: Unicode casefold substring across record_id, name, Summary, and normalized full content. Query, type, authority, and status filters combine with AND. Sort is record_id ascending. Facets count the complete viewed revision and do not change with active query or filters.
algorithms.history: Creation is ordinal 1 against an empty parent. Entries sort by revision ordinal in the requested direction. Omitted direction means forward. A backward first page starts at the highest approved ordinal at or below the viewed revision. Changes sort by record_id then added, removed, content_changed, metadata_changed, authority_transition. Removed records link to the verified parent revision; added and retained records link to the changed revision. Only verified snapshot comparisons enter approved history. Workflow, audit, table-fact, Draft, and proposal-lifecycle events never enter it.
algorithms.get_query_serialization: Atlas GET requests use strict UTF-8 percent-decoded flat query parameters. Reject malformed percent encoding, unknown parameters, duplicate singleton parameters, empty required values, aliases, comma-packed repeated filters, invalid enums, invalid integers, and cursor reuse under a different binding. Every revision-bound request requires revision_id, revision_ordinal, and tree_digest. Record filters use repeatable type, authority, and status keys, then deduplicate and sort their decoded values before building the logical query. Limit is explicit and ranges from 1 through 100. History direction is forward or backward and defaults to forward only when omitted.
